message:
The 1.9 Hz first mode sits squarely in the walking resonance band so Setra-type and Human-Induced Vibration of Steel Structures (HiVoSS) comfort checks govern, Structural Dynamicist and Bridge Retrofit Engineer.

In plain words the bridge will resonate with normal walking so I set Maximum comfort below 0.5 metres per second squared, Medium comfort 0.5 to 1.0 metres per second squared, Minimum comfort 1.0 to 2.5 metres per second squared and Unacceptable above 2.5 metres per second squared, which is the band stated in the Low-Cost Angular-Velocity Measurements for Sustainable Dynamic Identification of Pedestrian Footbridges: A Case Study of the Footbridge in Gdynia (Poland) (E33) and the Case (E34), while 1.90 Hz falling in the 1.40 to 2.40 Hz walking range is stated in the Analysis of the dynamic characteristics and vibrational comfort of selected footbridges over the S7 national road (E36).

In plain words a dense crowd drives the bare deck far past unacceptable but the Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), brings it back to Medium comfort, verified over time by simulation not assertion. The Class III crowd of 0.5 pedestrians per square metre from the 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases (E35) gives 60 people from the crowd-count calculation (E40) on the 40 by 3 m deck, equivalent to 5.92 synchronized pedestrians from the equivalent-count calculation (E41) using the 10.8 times root damping times number rule from the same 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases (E35), times 280 N per pedestrian from the Vibration Serviceability Assessment of a Historic Suspension Footbridge (E32) giving about 1.66 kN resonant force, which gives 8.28 metres per second squared bare from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) or 0.844 g almost a body weight and clearly outside everyday footbridge feel, falling to 0.668 metres per second squared with effective damping from the retrofitted-acceleration calculation (E44) and settling at 0.67 metres per second squared by 15 s in the crowd build-up simulation (E45).

In plain words holding Maximum comfort below 0.5 metres per second squared instead of accepting 0.67 metres per second squared costs more damper mass, more units and harder under-deck maintenance for little perceived gain. The 37 viscous plus 52 tuned-mass retrofit precedent that kept the silhouette by working under the deck is described in the Millennium Bridge, London (E39), and the emphasis of pedestrian dampers on human comfort serviceability is described in the Viscous Fluid Dampers for Bridges Market (E38), so I accept Medium comfort 0.5 to 1.0 metres per second squared as the retrofit target with below-soffit hardware that needs designed access, with the single-pedestrian 180 N harmonic basis from the FACTA UNIVERSITATIS — 2002 (E37) retained as the light-traffic check.

My position is not ready, because the Manager has not yet selected between Maximum and Medium comfort and the maintenance-access provision is still open.
